newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan central bank backs opening offshore futures.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan central bank backs opening offshore futures.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank said on Saturday it has decided to "cautiously support" allowing Taiwanese to trade offshore Taiwan stock index futures that were launched on January 9 by exchanges in Singapore and Chicago.

"The central bank, after thorough evaluation, has decided to cautiously support (allowing Taiwan's citizens to trade the offshore futures) because they can add risk-avoiding channels for stock investors," the bank said in a statement.

The bank said it was replying to a Finance Ministry request for the bank's opinion on whether to allow locals to trade the Taiwan stock index futures on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange and Singapore International Monetary Exchange.

In mid-January, soon after the CME and SIMEX started trading the Taiwan futures, Taiwan Finance Minister Paul Chiu and Central Bank Governor Sheu Yuan-dong said they regarded the offshore futures trading as "positive".
"We hold a positive view but we will monitor them for a period of time," Chiu said at the time.

Taiwan, keen to develop its own local futures trading, has stopped short of branding the CME and SIMEX as hostile rivals but has withheld technical cooperation and threatened to cut off access to crucial stock-price data.

Regulators said in early January that the launch of Taiwan's own futures exchange would have to be postponed to 1998 from an original target of October 1997, citing legislative bickering that has held up passage of a Futures Trading Law.
The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) also announced a half-year grace period during which it will monitor the offshore rivals but not interfere with their operations.
With Taiwan investors forced to stay on the sidelines, trading of the Taiwan stock-index futures on the two offshore exchanges has been slow.
San Francisco's Pacific Stock Exchange also launched trading of Taiwan stock-index options on January 9.
